content:
As previously mentioned earlier this year, Google Chrome has now switched to a biweekly release cycle.

In the past, Chrome had a major "milestone" update every four weeks, such as jumping from version 100 to version 101. Before 2021, Google used a six-week update cycle.

The change to releasing major updates every two weeks is aimed at "delivering new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes more quickly." Each update will contain less content, but the release frequency will increase accordingly.

Google stated that this "accelerated release cadence is good for the entire web." Developers will be able to "roll out modern web features more steadily, as deployment windows are tighter, interoperability updates reach users faster, and security improvements can be delivered across platforms more quickly." The smaller "scope" of each release will also make "regression isolation faster."

On the security front, Google said that in the face of rapidly evolving threats brought about by the rise of artificial intelligence, this change will help "respond to rapidly evolving threats."

For enterprise customers, Chrome offers an "Extended Stable" channel that updates every eight weeks—for example, after Chrome 156, it will jump to version 160. Google noted that most enterprise users should use the Stable version that updates every two weeks.

Chrome 153 is rolling out starting today, covering desktop, Android, and iOS platforms. Version 154 will be released on September 22.
